prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: what is the total purchase value of 1 to 31 December 2025, by event_date, for each first-touch medium? Read the value parameter from whichever number slot holds it: int_value on some purchases, double_value on others. Every purchase counts, one whose payment was later refunded included. The medium is traffic_source.medium, how the visitor first arrived; direct traffic shows as (none). Return medium and purchase_value, in euros. Return one row for each medium with a purchase. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check which slot of the value parameter the total reads.
Some purchases carry the amount in int_value, so read every number slot and take the one that is filled.
starter_sql:
WITH purchases AS (
  -- one row per purchase from 1 to 31 December 2025
  SELECT traffic_source.medium AS medium,
    list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'value')[1].value AS v
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251231'
)
SELECT medium, SUM(v.double_value) AS purchase_value
FROM purchases
GROUP BY medium
why_this_works: COALESCE over every number slot finds the amount whichever slot the tag filled, so no purchase drops out of the total.
